baseline_models.focus_anchor: The chain joins baddalu, ni'mat Allah, kufran, ahallu, qawmahum, and dar al-bawar.
baseline_models.mechanism: A received good is actively replaced or recast as concealment of that very good; the agents then make the consequence communal by settling their own people at an endpoint of failure.

activation_trace.role: Replacement supplies the operative exchange by which one condition is put in another's place.
Benefaction and good condition supply the positive term that is displaced.
Concealing or denying a benefit identifies the replacement as suppression of the gift's acknowledged status.
Caused settlement turns the exchange into a transitive placement of other people.
The people-group makes the damage social rather than confined to the exchangers.
Destruction and invalidation name the terminal condition produced by the placement.

changed_reading.before: The ayah reports that some people disbelieved and were punished.
changed_reading.after: The ayah depicts an active conversion of acknowledged benefit into its concealment, followed by leaders making that conversion the dwelling-condition of their community.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causative ahallu acts upon qawmahum and terminates in dar al-bawar.
baseline_models.mechanism: Those attached to a people as its governors and supports fail that role: instead of maintaining what lets communal life stand, they install the group inside an enclosing, unproductive order.

activation_trace.role: Good condition supplies the communal resource that stewardship should preserve.
Making others settle supplies the leaders' habitat-forming action.
Care, preservation, and governance expose the social duty inverted by the agents.
The support by which life stands turns the people's destination into a question of sustaining infrastructure.
An adverse turn enclosing a people gives the dwelling its systemic rather than merely architectural force.
Empty uncultivated land supplies an image of a habitat unable to yield communal life.

changed_reading.before: The agents merely accompany their people to a bad place.
changed_reading.after: The agents are failed stewards whose choices manufacture the social habitat in which their people can no longer stand or flourish.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Alam tara opens a visible and deliberative chain from substitution to communal settlement.
baseline_models.mechanism: The opening is not decorative: it calls the reader to inspect a causal case, combining perceptual recognition with considered judgment about how altered benefit becomes a public destination.

activation_trace.role: Alerting inquiry makes the following actors and consequences an evidentiary case.
Reflection and judgment extend seeing beyond bare optical notice.
The split mapping's deliberation image reinforces a considered reading of the displayed case.
Change of form supplies the first observable transformation in the causal chain.
A consequence becoming due or falling supplies the chain's visible outcome.

changed_reading.before: Have you not seen is a conventional rhetorical opening.
changed_reading.after: Have you not seen commissions a forensic reading of the social conversion: identify the actors, the altered good, and the destination they make fall upon others.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeatedly gives communal movement a positive vector: extraction from enclosing darkness, remembered rescue, and promised resettlement. The focus leaders reverse that vector, converting the remembered benefit into a counter-settlement at ruin.

activation_trace.role: The focus benefit is the good condition whose contextual history can now be specified.
The focus causative settlement anchors the reversal in the leaders' placement of their people.
Passage outward supplies the surah's initial emancipatory direction.
A community is explicitly the object of commanded extraction, matching the focus's communal object.
The remembered divine benefit is embedded in a concrete communal rescue sequence.
Deliverance by separation gives the remembered benefit an outbound rescuing force.
Threatened forced exit shows hostile rulers manipulating communal location.
Promised habitation supplies the positive counterpart to the focus leaders' destructive settlement.

structural_cues: 14:1 and 14:5 repeat movement from darkness toward light as the commanded communal trajectory.
14:6 places remembrance of divine benefit inside rescue from imposed harm.
14:13-14 oppose rulers' threatened expulsion to a promised resettlement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies extraction, rescue, forced expulsion, and resettlement; I supply the arrow that 14:28's leaders reverse that emancipatory trajectory; alternatively, the sequence may be contrastive rather than one continuous migration mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The leaders place their people in an unspecified ruin.
changed_reading.after: The leaders perform a counter-exodus: they reverse a remembered movement out of oppression and make their people settle at the failed endpoint.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's market-stagnation branch of bawar becomes a model of unrealizable return: what was worked for and acquired is reduced to residue and dispersed, leaving no usable claim on the gain.

activation_trace.role: Stagnation until spoilage supplies the focus anchor for an economy whose value no longer clears.
Burn residue supplies the material state of former work after its usable value is destroyed.
A violent dispersing force prevents even the residue from being retained.
Seeking and obtaining benefit names the acquisition over which the actors finally have no control.

structural_cues: 14:18 compares the disbelievers' works to ash scattered on a violently windy day.
The same ayah denies their ability to retain anything from what they acquired.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies spoiled-market bawar, acquired benefit, ash, and dispersal; I supply the arrow from unusable residue to a nonclearing economy; alternatively, the image may mark futility without any economic mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Dar al-bawar is simply a place where destruction occurs.
changed_reading.after: Dar al-bawar can also be a failed value-system in which labor and acquisition yield no retainable return.

context_deltas.mechanism: The causative force of ahallu remains asymmetrical leadership, but the later dispute prevents a model of mechanically passive followers: status leaders are followed, calls are answered, and persons remain answerable for their response.

activation_trace.role: Causing others to settle preserves the focus leaders' real directional agency.
The leaders' own people remain the social body affected by that direction.
Elevated status and leadership identify the socially dominant side of the dispute.
Allegiance and sequence supply the followers' active attachment to those above them.
A call that inclines by speech supplies influence without irresistible compulsion.
Answering speech supplies the followers' responsive participation.
The self as the person's own identity keeps responsibility located in each responder.

structural_cues: 14:21 stages weak followers asking dominant figures to avert the consequence.
14:22 denies coercive authority while preserving invitation, response, and self-blame.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies dominance, allegiance, calling, answering, and self-blame; I supply an asymmetrical but distributed agency model for ahallu qawmahum; alternatively, the later dialogue may diagnose only one afterlife dispute rather than every leader-community relation.

changed_reading.before: The people are inert cargo whom leaders alone deposit in ruin.
changed_reading.after: The leaders construct and promote the destination, while followers inhabit it through responsive allegiance; communal causation is unequal but not mechanically one-sided.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding tree sequence turns substitution and settlement into ecological governance: a sound order has root, stability, and recurring yield, whereas a corrupt order is extracted whole from its root and has no stable base. The focus leaders move their people from the first kind of system into the second.

activation_trace.role: Recasting a thing's condition supplies the focus's system-level transformation.
Making a community settle gives the ecological transformation a social habitat.
Unworked empty land supplies the focus endpoint's failure to cultivate or yield.
A sustaining base supplies the productive order's rooted foundation.
Durable stability keeps the rooted order in place.
Recurring tree-yield makes stability productive rather than static.
Whole-root extraction supplies the destructive inverse of stable cultivation.
Denied stability leaves the corrupt growth without a place from which to endure.
Active strengthening links the arboreal stability to the people preserved by the firm saying.

structural_cues: 14:24-25 joins fixed root, high branch, and recurrent yield.
14:26 reverses every element: corrupt growth is uprooted and lacks stability.
14:27 carries the stability vocabulary from the tree image into the treatment of people immediately before 14:28.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies rooted yield, total uprooting, denied stability, and then communal settlement; I supply the arrow that the leaders' substitution is a social transplant from productive to barren order; alternatively, the tree contrast may remain a saying-level analogy rather than a governance ecology.

changed_reading.before: The leaders exchange one belief for another and later reach ruin.
changed_reading.after: The leaders uproot the productive order that sustains their people and transplant them into a social ecology with no stable base or recurring yield.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next two ayat resolve both endpoint and route: the bad settlement is named with Jahannam, while rival objects enable misdirection from a traversable way until the people's destination is fire.

activation_trace.role: Caused settlement anchors the route in a destination imposed on the community.
Ruin and invalidation supply the destination's defining condition.
A condemned place of settlement directly specifies the focus dwelling's terminal stability.
A rival counterpart supplies the substituted orientation that initiates divergence.
Deviation from guidance supplies the leaders' routing action.
A traversable extended way makes misguidance a departure from an actual route.
Becoming toward an endpoint turns the leaders' influence into directed arrival.
Kindled fire supplies the route's explicitly named destination.

structural_cues: 14:29 immediately apposes Jahannam, entry into it, and a condemned settlement.
14:30 orders rival-making, misdirection from a path, temporary enjoyment, and destination in fire.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a condemned settlement followed by rival-making, path-deviation, endpoint, and fire; I supply the causal route connecting these to ahallu; alternatively, 14:29 may identify the focus dwelling without requiring every routing step inferred from 14:30.

changed_reading.before: Dar al-bawar is an abstract state of failure.
changed_reading.after: Dar al-bawar is both the explicitly fiery endpoint and the completed route produced by rival orientation and communal misdirection.

context_deltas.mechanism: Blessing expands from a possessed item into a circulating provision-system: allotted sustenance arrives through created channels, matures as fruit, and is sent outward in expenditure. Kufr covers both source and flow, converting a renewable circuit into the dead-end economy of bawar.

activation_trace.role: Benefaction and good condition anchor the context's provision network in the focus blessing.
Concealment of benefit interrupts acknowledgment of the network's source.
Stagnation until spoilage supplies the result when provision no longer circulates.
Wealth going outward in expenditure supplies the circuit's commanded social outflow.
An allotted gift supplies the network's incoming distribution.
Mature fruit makes the distributed provision a recurring material yield.
The context again names the entire uncountable supply as divine benefit.
Intensive ingratitude closes the sequence by covering the very benefit just declared beyond tally.

structural_cues: 14:31 joins established worship to expenditure before a day with no sale or friendship.
14:32-33 presents water, fruit, transport, rivers, sun, moon, night, and day as coordinated provisions.
14:34 says the divine benefit cannot be exhaustively counted and closes with intensified human ingratitude.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies outgoing expenditure, allotted sustenance, mature yield, uncountable benefit, and ingratitude; I supply the circuit model and the arrow from concealment to stagnation; alternatively, these may be parallel duties and gifts rather than one circulation system.

changed_reading.before: The exchanged blessing is a single possession that leaders reject.
changed_reading.after: The exchanged blessing is the whole renewable infrastructure of received and shared provision; covering it turns circulation into spoilage and social dead end.

context_deltas.mechanism: A leader can settle his descendants in a valley explicitly lacking cultivation without making it dar al-bawar. Orientation to the protected house, maintained worship, attracted hearts, provision, fruit, and gratitude can turn harsh geography into viable communal life; ruin therefore names a failed relational order, not barrenness alone.

activation_trace.role: The focus act of settling a people anchors the comparison between two kinds of emplacement.
Uncultivated empty land supplies the spatial reading that the counterexample tests and limits.
Deliberate habitation supplies a positive leader-to-descendants counterpart to ahallu qawmahum.
A valley as a channel supplies objectively severe terrain rather than an already flourishing site.
The explicitly absent cultivation sharpens the site's resemblance to the focus's barren-land branch.
A sheltering dwelling supplies the settlement's orienting center.
Maintaining and caring for an undertaking gives worship a community-sustaining function.
Requested allotted provision supplies an incoming life-supporting flow.
Mature fruit supplies productive yield despite the valley's initial lack of cultivation.
Recognition of benefit closes the positive settlement mechanism with the inverse of kufr.

structural_cues: 14:37 explicitly combines settlement of descendants with a valley lacking cultivation.
The same ayah orders the site around the protected house, worship, social attraction, provision, fruit, and gratitude.
This sequence follows 14:34's uncountable benefit and intensive ingratitude.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two leader-made settlements, one named ruin and one materially barren yet provision-oriented; I supply the contrast that orientation and sustaining flows distinguish them; alternatively, 14:37 may be an exceptional sacred settlement rather than a general habitat model.

changed_reading.before: The barren-land branch makes dar al-bawar equivalent to physically uncultivated terrain.
changed_reading.after: Physical barrenness is not sufficient for ruin: dar al-bawar is a settlement whose leaders sever orientation, provision, and gratitude, while even an unplanted valley can become life-bearing under the opposite pattern.

context_deltas.mechanism: The command to see gains a historical-material register: later addressees inhabit the residences of earlier self-wrongers, and their outcome has been made clear through examples. Dar al-bawar can therefore be an inherited ruin that visibly teaches how social orders fail.

activation_trace.role: Alerting inquiry anchors the later dwellings and examples as evidence the reader must inspect.
Empty dwellings and uncultivated land make ruin materially legible across generations.
Eyes fixed in sight intensify the surah's demand that consequence become visible.
Living in predecessors' residences turns past wrongdoing into an occupied material record.
Manifest disclosure makes the predecessors' outcome available for recognition.
An example functioning as warning converts visible remains into instruction.

structural_cues: 14:42 denies divine inattention and delays the wrongdoers to a day of fixed gaze.
14:45 says the addressees lived in the residences of people who wronged themselves.
14:45 joins that habitation to clarified action and presented examples.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies seeing, inherited residences, disclosure, and warning-examples; I supply the archaeological arrow from those residences to dar al-bawar as visible social aftermath; alternatively, the residences may function rhetorically without being literal ruins.

changed_reading.before: Have you not seen asks for abstract moral recognition of a future abode.
changed_reading.after: Have you not seen also asks the reader to recognize ruin in inhabited historical evidence: failed social worlds leave dwellings that later communities can inspect.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same change-root later marks a cosmic transformation, but that change culminates in emergence before the one overpowering God. Human change in the focus culminates in covering; divine change culminates in exposure. The fault is therefore not transformation as such but a counterfeit remaking that conceals source and installs false destination.

activation_trace.role: Alteration of condition anchors the human transformation whose direction is under examination.
Covering supplies the human transformation's concealmentward direction.
A second replacement supplies the formal echo at cosmic scale.
Alteration or exchange by another state confirms that the later scene is genuine transformation.
Emergence and uncovering give the divine transformation an exposureward direction.
Unshared divine oneness supplies the authority before which the transformed order is exposed.
Overpowering from above supplies the decisive authority absent from the leaders' counterfeit remaking.

structural_cues: 14:48 repeats the focus change-root in a transformation of earth and heavens.
The transformed scene immediately proceeds to universal emergence before the one overpowering God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated change, focus-covering, later emergence, oneness, and overpowering authority; I supply the opposition between counterfeit concealment and authoritative disclosure; alternatively, the shared root may mark two transformations without a deliberate moral contrast.

changed_reading.before: Baddalu is blameworthy simply because it denotes change.
changed_reading.after: The leaders' change is blameworthy because it usurps direction and conceals the giver; the later divine change exposes all agents and destinations before singular authority.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it treats two distant covering images as a material chiasm; it remains anchored in the focus k-f-r covering branch and the resumed seeing construction, while 14:50 supplies an actual covering of faces. Downstream prose should call it a lexical-material echo, not assert that the two coverings are semantically identical.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Kufran can activate literal covering, while alam tara makes visibility integral to the focus.

activation_trace.role: A covering placed over something supplies the agents' initial concealment of benefit.
Perceptual and insightful seeing makes concealment itself the object of disclosure.
Resumed seeing turns the earlier concealed agents into an explicitly visible scene.
An overlying cover supplies the involuntary covering that returns upon the exposed figures.
The visible face localizes the returned covering on the person's exposed front.
Kindled fire supplies the covering material and completes the visible reversal.

changed_reading.before: The agents cover the blessing and later receive an unrelated punishment.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the covering rebounds: those who made benefit invisible are made visible, and an involuntary fiery cover occupies their exposed faces.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the non-dominant h-l-y mapping under the focus h-l-l occurrence and is form-distant from ordinary caused-settlement. It remains packet-valid because that exact mapped branch contributes dried vegetation and converges with the focus's uncultivated bawar branch plus the adjacent uprooted-tree sequence. Downstream prose should retain it only as a botanical secondary resonance.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The exact ahallu occurrence has a packet-supplied h-l-y branch of dried vegetation beside bawar as uncultivated land.

activation_trace.role: Dried crop or vegetation supplies a form-distant image of what the people become under destructive emplacement.
Uncultivated empty land supplies the habitat in which the social growth dries out.
The living stemmed tree supplies the productive organism against which desiccation is read.
Extraction whole from the root supplies the loss of life-support preceding the dried condition.

changed_reading.before: The people are moved into an external ruined location.
changed_reading.after: As a contained botanical resonance, the destructive transplant also dries the communal organism itself: uprooted people become failed growth within failed land.

strongest_changes: The focus becomes a counter-exodus in which leaders reverse remembered rescue and resettlement into communal emplacement at ruin.
The adjacent rooted-tree sequence recasts the exchange as uprooting a productive social ecology and transplanting people into a system without stable yield.
The barren-valley settlement shows that harsh geography is not itself dar al-bawar; failed orientation, provision, gratitude, and stewardship make the ruin.
The following ayat resolve the route through rival orientation and misguidance, and the destination as a condemned fiery settlement.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context activated a habitat-and-circulation reading without erasing the direct afterlife destination: blessing is a communal support system, leaders shape where a people can stand, and ruin is simultaneously social process, visible historical aftermath, and final arrival.
remaining_uncertainties: The economic reading of bawar may be a secondary branch resonance rather than the governing sense.
The tree mechanism may describe sayings first and social governance only by analogy.
The contrast between human and divine substitution in 14:48 is structurally suggestive but remains exploratory.
The covering reversal and dried-transplant outliers require explicit qualification because they depend on cross-domain or non-dominant branches.
